kind._comment: Keyed by the AST node kind string.

left.description:
Declares that an endpoint or message direction is `left`.

- In a channel class, `left` messages are sent by the left endpoint.
- In a process argument, `left` names the role this process plays on the channel.

right.description:
Declares that an endpoint or message direction is `right`.

- In a channel class, `right` messages are sent by the right endpoint.
- In a process argument, `right` names the role this process plays on the channel.

assigned by.description:
Part of a `shared` variable declaration; names the thread index (zero-based) that is responsible for writing the shared variable.

**Example:**

```anvil
shared(#1) result assigned by 0;
```

generate.description:
Compile-time parallel loop unrolling. Instantiates the body expression once for each value of the loop variable, with all instances running concurrently (joined with `;`).

**Example:**

```anvil
generate (i : 0, 3, 1) {
    send eps[i].req(data[i])
}
```

generate_seq.description:
Compile-time sequential loop unrolling. Instantiates the body expression once for each value of the loop variable, with all instances chained sequentially (with `>>`).

**Example:**

```anvil
generate_seq (i : 0, 3, 1) {
    send ep.req(data[i])
}
```

void.description: The unit type. Also expressed as an empty tuple `()`.

recursive.description:
Starts a recursive thread inside a process. Unlike `loop`, the restart point is explicit - the `recurse` expression causes the thread to restart from the beginning. This allows pipelining and conditional restart.

**Example:**

```anvil
recursive {
    let x = recv ep.req >>
    send ep.resp(x) >>
    recurse
}
```

else.description: The else branch of an `if` expression or `try` expression, evaluated when the condition is false or the operation is not immediately ready.

in.description:
Set-membership test. Returns a truthy value if the left operand equals any element in the right-hand set literal.

**Example:**

```anvil
if state in {State::Idle, State::Done} { /* ... */ }
```

with.description:
Struct update syntax. Creates a copy of an existing struct value with one or more fields overridden.

**Example:**

```anvil
Coord::{ base with x = 8'd5 }
```

builtInKeywordCompletions._comment_pact: Pact extensions: session types, interfaces, pools, offers, and one-way (instantaneous) messages.

interface.description:
Declares an **interface**: a named session type describing the order and timing of messages over a list of endpoints.

A process takes interfaces instead of endpoint arguments (`proc p(i1, i2)`); the endpoints they name become available in its body, and the *i*-th interface constrains the *i*-th thread. Pools instantiate interfaces to check that processes are compatible.

Optional data-type parameters go **before** the name. There is no terminator: a trailing `;` is read as sequencing and causes a syntax error.

**Example:**

```anvil
interface left_if (ep : left ch) = ep.req ; ep.ack ; #1
interface <T : type> data_if (ep : left ch<T>) = ep.req

proc worker(left_if) {
    loop { let x = recv ep.req >> send ep.ack(1'd1) >> cycle 1 }
}
```

protocol.description:
Attaches a channel-local session type to a channel class. It goes last in the `chan` body, with **no comma** after the final message. The session type refers to the endpoint by the name of the process argument that uses the channel.

**Example:**

```anvil
chan ch {
    left req : (logic@#1),
    right ack : (logic@#1)
    protocol :: (ep.req ; ep.ack)
}
```

xoffer.description:
An **exclusive offer**: takes exactly one of its arms. Arms use the same forms as `offer`. Blocking and instantaneous arms cannot be mixed, and an optional `else { e }`, allowed only with instantaneous arms, runs when none is available.

An optional selector wire chooses which arm wins when several are ready: `xoffer sel { ... }` (or `xoffer rotate sel`) tries arm `sel + i` at step `i`; `xoffer tree sel` tries arm `sel XOR i`, as a binary-tree round-robin arbiter.

Corresponds to `^( ... )` / `⨁( ... )` in session types.

**Example:**

```anvil
xoffer {
    x = recv ep.req => cycle 5,
    y = recv ep.ack => cycle 3
} >> cycle 1
```

isend.description:
An **instantaneous send**: like `send`, but with a one-way handshake. The sender does not wait for the receiver to acknowledge.

**Example:**

```anvil
isend ep.req(2'd1) >> cycle 1
```

irecv.description:
An **instantaneous receive**: like `recv`, but with a one-way handshake. The receiver does not acknowledge the sender.

**Example:**

```anvil
let v = irecv ep.req >> cycle 1
```

try isend.description:
Attempts an instantaneous send (`isend`) and branches on whether it happened this cycle.

**Example:**

```anvil
try isend o.out(1'd1) { cycle 1 } else { cycle 2 }
```

try irecv.description:
Attempts an instantaneous receive (`irecv`) and branches on whether a value arrived this cycle.

**Example:**

```anvil
try x = irecv ep.req { dprint "got %d" (x) >> cycle 1 } else { cycle 1 }
```

description:
Defines a **recursive session type** `rec X . s`, where `X` inside `s` refers back to the whole type. `μ X . s` is equivalent.

The body binds a single atom, so parenthesize it: `rec X . (ep.req ; X)` rather than `rec X . ep.req ; X`.

**Example:**

```anvil
interface i1 (ep : left ch) = #1 ; rec X . (ep.req + (#1 ; X)) ; #1
```

forall.description:
A **quantified session type** over an integer range, for indexed endpoints such as `ep[i]`. `∀` is equivalent, and `∈` may replace `:`.

`forall (i : [a..b]) OP { s }` combines the copies of `s` with `OP`: `+`/`∑` (choice) or `||`/`∏` (parallel). With `&`/`⋀` or `^`/`⨁`, the braces hold offer arms instead.

Bounds must be integer literals. Indices can be excluded with `not 2` or `not (2, 4)`.

**Example:**

```anvil
forall (i : [1..3] not 2) + { ep[i].req ; #1 }
∀ (i ∈ [1..3]) ⨁ { ep[i].req : #1, * : #3 }
```

not.description:
Excludes indices from a `forall` range: `not 2` or `not (2, 4)`. ` ̸` is equivalent.

**Example:**

```anvil
forall (i : [1..5] not (2, 4)) || { ep[i].data ; #1 }
```

F.description:
The **future** operator in session types: `F s` means `s` happens at some later point rather than immediately. `F` binds tighter than every binary session operator and is a reserved word.

**Example:**

```anvil
interface mem_itfc (rd : right read_ch) = rd.req ; F #rd.res ; #1
```

timingCompletions._comment: Fixed completion entries for the timing annotation heuristic context (inside a channel class message definition after '@'). Split into two sub-sections: 'lifetime' entries appear after the first '@' inside the payload parentheses, and 'sync' entries appear after the closing ')' when adding a sync-mode annotation.

#N.description: **Fixed lifetime**: The message is available for `N` cycles when sent/received.

%s.description: **Relative lifetime**: The message is available for the same number of cycles as `%s`.

%s+N.description: **Relative lifetime**: The message is available for the duration of the lifetime of `%s`, offset by `N` cycles.

eternal.description: **Eternal lifetime**: The message is available indefinitely when sent/received.

#N.description:
**Static synchronization**: The message is sent/received every `N` cycles (beginning on cycle `N`).

**Example:**

```anvil
@#2 // every 2nd cycle
    // (i.e., 2nd, 4th, 6th, ...)
```

#I~N.description:
**Static synchronization**: The message is sent/received every `N` cycles (beginning on cycle `I`).

**Example:**

```anvil
@#1~3 // every 3rd cycle, beginning cycle 1
      // (i.e., 1st, 4th, 7th, ...)
```

dyn.description: **Dynamic synchronization**: The sender and receiver synchronize on messages via handshaking signals.

#%s.description: **Dependent synchronization**: The message is sent/received at the same time as the referenced message `%s`.

#%s+N.description: **Dependent synchronization**: The message is sent/received `N` cycles after the referenced message `%s`.

unicodeOperators._comment: Unicode session-type operators, keyed by the symbol. Typing a backslash followed by a trigger (e.g. \sum) offers the symbol. Every symbol has an ASCII equivalent.

∑.description:
**N-ary internal choice** in session types: `∑(s1, s2, ...)` is `s1 + s2 + ...`. Also the choice operator of `forall`.

```anvil
∑(ep.req, ep.ack ; #1)
```

∏.description:
**N-ary parallel composition** in session types: `∏(s1, s2, ...)` is `s1 || s2 || ...`. Also the parallel operator of `forall`.

```anvil
∀ (i ∈ [1..3]) ∏ { ep[i].data ; #1 }
```

⋀.description:
**Offer** in session types: `⋀(arms)` waits for the triggers of its arms, any of which may be taken together. `⋀(arms).(cases)` continues by the exact set of arms taken. Arms are `ep.m : cont`, `#ep.m`, `* : cont` (wildcard), `$ s` (terminal), or `{ep.a, ep.b} : cont`.

```anvil
⋀(ep.m1 : ep.m2, * : ep.m3)
```

⨁.description:
**Exclusive offer** in session types: `⨁(arms)` takes exactly one of its arms. Arms use the same forms as `⋀`.

```anvil
rec X . ⨁(#ep.req, * : #1 ; X)
```

∀.description:
**Quantifier** over an integer range: `∀ (i ∈ [a..b]) OP { s }` combines copies of `s` for each `i` with `∑`, `∏`, `⋀` or `⨁`.

```anvil
∀ (i ∈ [1..5] ̸ (2,4)) ∏ { ep[i].data ; #1 }
```

∈.description: Binds a `∀` index to a range: `∀ (i ∈ [1..3]) ...`.

μ.description:
**Recursion**: `μ X . s` in session types, or `μ X { e }` in expressions (restarted by `recurse X`). Parenthesize session-type bodies: `μ X . (ep.req ; X)`.

```anvil
interface i1 (ep : left ch) = #1 ; μ X . (ep.req + (#1 ; X)) ; #1
```

̸.description: Excludes indices from a `∀` range: `[1..5] ̸ (2,4)` or `[1..5] ̸2`. The symbol is lexed as **exactly one space** followed by U+0338, so it must not be preceded by extra whitespace.
